name: netdust-devops
description: 0.7.2: make smoke env=E — commands.smoke run against environments.E.url with SMOKE_URL/SMOKE_ENV set, read-only so no terminal and no confirm; deploy and ship close by naming it; the wp template declares the Playwright @smoke runner. 0.7.1: four doors onto a server, closed. rollback refuses by name over git-push — it rsynced nothing and stamped the ledger anyway (daan, netdust, stride). deploy env=production redeploys a shipped commit and releases nothing: ship stamps shipped/production in the same atomic push as the branch, the gate lets production take only that commit or the one deployed/production names, and it runs behind both backups. A hotfix/* branch carrying a promote: merge is refused — the name was the only check. The deploy gate wants origin's tip, not any commit origin contains: a checkout behind origin deployed the older commit and stamped it. 0.7.0: the simple flow — staging is the release. Seven verbs replace the old flow: feature, hotfix, save, promote, unpromote, gate, ship. No engine script, no custom ref namespace, no separate release branch: promote rebuilds staging in a throwaway worktree from origin/<production> plus every feature already there, each a --no-ff merge; ship refuses unless HEAD, origin/staging and the deployed ledger name the same commit, then runs the gate itself before the typed confirmation. A project still declaring environments.development.branch is refused by name and told the restore — `git checkout <commit before the update> -- Makefile.netdust mk scripts .netdust-devops`. A project with its own CLI variable declares it before the include as `_CLI_EXTRA := NAME`. flow-test.sh exercises every verb and refusal against a bare origin, no server contacted. 0.6.3: three project-local fixes reach the core. Over git-push the payload lives in git, so ship no longer archives nothing and refuses (daan's first production ship stalled on that). The vendored deploy-test accepts a rung declared before its server exists — production with a branch and no path, a branch-only development — instead of failing five checks on the shape the skill prescribes. And it asserts the mail-block exclude on rsync projects. dist/VERSION now tracks the release so make doctor can actually say a project is behind. 0.6.2: ship leaves from the production branch itself; the retired merge-forward verb used to leave you on the review rung, and ship then refused by name ('production deploys from master — you are on develop'), which sent the human to raw git. _ship-branch now runs right after the tty check: clean tree required, checkout of the production branch, fast-forward from origin, refuse on divergence. The single source of truth for Netdust devops: the branch flow, the deploy gate and ledger, and the project/fleet contract. Ships a stack-split Makefile core (mk/wp, statamic, node, generic) that every project vendors rather than copies, so a fix made once reaches every project and `make doctor` names any project that is behind or edited in place. Owns site.yml schema 2 — environments: binds a branch to a server, and nothing else may. Replaces the flow half of netdust-core:dev-stack and both /deploy commands.
